title: Handle Rust failure explicitly
why: unwrap terminates the process when a Result or Option is not successful.
suggestion: Propagate the error, handle each variant, or document why failure is impossible.
limitations: The rule uses masked source tokens and does not perform Rust type resolution.

Conventional test modules, lint-allowed items, literal or fully escaped regex construction, regex capture group zero (including chains of capture iterators), guarded Option and collection access, infallible formatting into a proven String, literal parsing, positive literal NonZero construction, NUL-free CString literals and unambiguous same-file root string constants, attached function panic contracts, generated catalog invariants, and documented local invariants are excluded. Chained capture iterators establish only group zero; explicit numbered and named groups are not inferred across different patterns.

Group zero is also proven for direct iter().flat_map(|pattern| pattern.captures_iter(...)) loops at the first source use of an immutable parameter explicitly typed &[Regex] or &[&Regex], including regex::Regex paths. Prior parameter reuse, custom or unknown collection types, mutable parameter bindings, shadowed bindings, block callbacks, transformed callback results, and nonzero capture groups are not inferred by this proof.

Local guards include else-if Option checks and exact chars().count() == 1 checks with matching receivers and no intervening receiver or parent reuse; disjoint sibling fields may change. The first character of a fresh case-mapping iterator is excluded only for a local immutable binding obtained directly from chars().next().unwrap()/expect().

Standalone same-brace-scope is_none()/is_err() guards followed by an unconditional return exclude later unwrap/expect calls on the same receiver, including as_ref()/as_deref()/as_mut()/as_deref_mut() and exact shadow-binding initializers. Flat failure disjunctions are supported only when later operands do not reuse the receiver or its parent. Unlabeled continue/break also prove fallthrough when the guard and use are directly in the same loop body; preceding nested statements may not replace the terminal exit. Labeled loops, nested use scopes, and delayed callbacks are not inferred. Positive is_ok() conjuncts use the same receiver-invalidation boundaries as is_some().

Exact len() == 1 or !is_empty() guards prove first/last, mutable first/last, pop/pop_front, and the next element of fresh iter/iter_mut/keys/values/values_mut iterators. Matching guarded braced match arms, conjunctions, and direct while bodies are supported; receiver or parent reuse in a later conjunct or body invalidates the proof. A single copied()/cloned() adapter preserves presence; filtering, callbacks, dynamic indices, unrecognized methods, nested scopes, and arbitrary collection or iterator implementations are not resolved.

CString constant resolution excludes nested modules, ambiguous declarations, name-imports, glob imports, nonliteral initializers, and unsupported escapes. Unconditionally compiled modules remain production source even when their names or documentation describe test helpers.

Top-level if-condition is_some()/is_ok() conjunctions and is_none()/is_err() disjunctions also prove presence within a later operand. Opposite boolean operators, intervening receiver reuse, and callbacks invalidate this local proof; arbitrary expression contexts and nested parenthesized boolean trees are not resolved.

A direct same-brace-scope receiver assignment to Some(...) proves a later direct unwrap/expect or a supported reference adapter only without intervening receiver/parent reuse, shadowing, conditional assignment, or delayed callbacks. This does not establish arbitrary initializer, macro, lock-poisoning, custom method, or interprocedural invariants.

Multiline allow and expect lint attributes are honored over their attributed item or block; inner attributes stay within their enclosing scope. Unknown or malformed lint expectations do not suppress findings. Comments and string literals cannot introduce allowances or expectations. Panic contracts are scoped to the containing function, not nested or sibling functions.
An attached invariant comment can cover a multiline expression, but not a later expression across a completed statement or block.

A same-brace-scope let Some(...) = collection.first()/last()/first_mut()/last_mut() else { return ...; } proves later direct element access or fresh iteration on that collection, without receiver/parent reuse, shadowing, filtering, nested uses, or delayed callbacks. A successful pop guard does not prove another pop.

Fresh split()/rsplit() iterators always yield at least one segment, so direct next(), last(), and next_back() access is excluded. Terminator/whitespace splitters, intervening iterator adapters, and previously consumed iterators are not covered.

An exact standalone is_none() branch assigning Some(...) to the same receiver, including a single dereference assignment, proves presence after fallthrough. Alternative branches, conditional or transformed initialization, later receiver/parent reuse, shadowing, nested uses, and delayed callbacks invalidate the proof. Presence does not establish success of a Result stored inside the Option.

Attached literal doc attributes can declare the same panic policy as triple-slash documentation. Dynamic documentation expressions are not evaluated, and contracts stay within the documented function rather than nested or neighboring functions.
